Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the

18:6963-1973 

Indian Standard 

PICTORIAL MARKING ON PACKAGES 

CONTAINING PHOTOGRAPHIC MATERIALS 

SENSITIVE TO RADIANT ENERGY 



0. FOREWORD 

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards 
Institution on 28 May IQTS, after the draft finaHzed by the Cargo 
Marking, HandHng and Storage Sectional Committee had been approved 
by the Marine, Cargo Movement and Packaging Division Council. 

0.2 Photographic materials, such as films, plates and papers, are finding 
increasing use for medical and industrial purposes. Since these materials 
are sensitive towards heat and radioactive energy, they need be trans- 
ported and stored carefully. Pictorial markings are put to inform the 
handlers of such packages that the contents need special care. Visual 
effects have lasting impression on the human mind and are preferred to 
the written instructions which have its own problems because of the 
multilanguage character of our country. 

0.3 In the preparation of this standard considerable assistance has been 
derived from ISO/R 884-1968 ' Pictorial marking of transit packages 
containing photographic materials sensitive to radiant energy ', issued by 
International Organization for Standardization (ISO). 



1. SCOPE 

i.i This standard specifies the size and layout of the pictorial marking to 
be affixed on the exterior of packages containing unexposed and exposed 
but unprocessed photographic and radiographic films, plates and papers. 

2. PICTORIAL MARKING 

2.1 The pictorial marking shall be in the form of a stamp, stencil or 
label carrying the word ' FOTO ' in capital letters 40 to 50 m.m. high, 
superimposed on a simulated strip of motion-picture film not less than 
80 mm wide with perforation symbols along both edges as given on P 4. 



IS: 6963 -1973 

2.2 The pictorial marking shall signify the following: 

'Sensitized photographic or radiographic material; stow away from 
heat and radioactive sources '. 



FOTO
